§ 2Content

§ 3CDM AND SIMON COMMISSION

§ 4Socialism

  • Theory of Socialism was given by Karl Marx, he stated that "Only option to remove the rich classes from society is mass struggle".
  • Reason for Socialism: Russian Revolution in 1917.
  • In 1920, All India Trade Union Congress was formed by Lala Lajpat Rai, Joseph Baptista, N. M. Joshi.
  • N M Lokhande is known as the "Father of Trade Union Movement". He founded Bombay Mill Association.

§ 5Spread of Socialism and Communalism

  • Communist Party of India (CPI) was formed by M. N. Roy in Tashkent, Uzbekistan in 1920.
  • In 1924, the party was involved in Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case → People involved: S A Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shaukat Usmani, etc.
  • In 1925, CPI was formalised in Kanpur.
  • In 1929, Meerut Conspiracy Case occurred.

§ 6Novels and Books

  • Bandi Jeevan by: Sachin Sanyal.
  • Pather Dabi by: Sharat Chandra Chattopadhyay.
  • Philosophy of Bomb by: B. C. Vohra.

§ 7EVENTS AROUND INDIA

In Punjab-UP-Bihar

  • In 1924, Hindustan Republican Association was formed in Kanpur by Ram Prasad Bismil, J. C. Chatterjee, Sachin Sanyal.
  • In 1925, Kakori Incident/Kakori Train Robbery took place in Kakori, a village near Lucknow.
  • Participants who were hanged to death: Ashfaqullah Khan, Roshan Singh, Ram Prasad Bismil, and Rajendra Lahiri.
  • In 1926, Punjab Naujawan Bharat Sabha was formed by Bhagat Singh.
  • Bhagat Singh fully accepted Marxism.
  • Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) which was later transformed to Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) in 1928 at Feroz Shah Kotla by Chandra Shekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev.
  • In 1928, Lala Lajpat Rai protested against Simon Commission and recited slogan "Simon go back". He was hit by Scott during lathi charge due to which he died afterwards.
  • In 1928, Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Raj Guru killed Saunders instead of Scott mistakenly in Lahore to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai.
  • In 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt bombed Central Legislative Assembly.
  • Reason: To protest against "Public Safety Bill" (1928) as it was Anti-National (as said by Swaraj Party) and Trade Disputes Bill (1929).
  • Purpose: No to kill anyone but To Make Deaf Hear.
  • In 1929, Chandra Shekhar Azad was involved in the conspiracy to blow up Lord Irwin's train, unfortunately the plan failed.
  • Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev and Rajguru were tried in Lahore Conspiracy Case and were hanged on 23rd March 1931 (now celebrated as "Shaheed Diwas").

Note: 30 Jan, the day Gandhiji died is also celebrated as "Shaheed Diwas".

Book written by Bhagat Singh: "Why I Am an Atheist"

In Bengal

  • In 1930, Chittagong Armoury Raid was led by Surya Sen (also known as Master Da).
  • Women participants involved were: Pritilata Waddedar, Kalpana Dutta, Suniti Chanderi, Bina Das.
  • It is now known as Chandrashekhar Azad Park where he shot himself on 27 February 1931 in Allahabad

§ 8SIMON COMMISSION

  • Government of India Act 1919 was set to be reviewed by a Commission in 10 years but it announced the appointment of a Commission in just 8 years after the Act under the chairmanship of John Simon.

Note: Clement Attlee (who later became PM of Britain) was the member of Simon Commission.

  • In 1928, this Commission arrived in India which was a 7-membered Commission (all white and no Indians) → Revolt against it was set in motion with slogans "Simon Go Back" (term coined by "Yusuf Meherally").

§ 9Recommendations of Simon Commission

  • Abolition of dyarchy.
  • Federal system of government should be introduced in India.
  • Extended voting rights.
  • Separate Muslim electorate.
  • It rejected the separation of Sindh from Bombay.
  • The demand of frontier for equal status was also neglected.
  • It rejected 1/3rd Muslim seats in Central Assembly.

§ 10Madras Session of Congress of 1928

  • President: M. A. Ansari.
  • It was a special Session which passed a resolution, calling for boycott of Simon Commission.

§ 11Response to Simon Commission

  • The then Secretary, Birkenhead challenged the Indian leaders to draft their own Constitution
  • Congress set up a committee under the chairmanship of Motilal Nehru which presented Nehru Report.

§ 12Demands in Nehru Report

  1. 1. Rejected Separate Electorate.
  2. 2. Demand for Dominion status.
  3. 3. Linguistic provinces, 19 Fundamental Rights, and a Responsible Government.
  • Delhi Proposals were given by Muslim League (1927).
  • Jinnah presented his 14 points (1929). Ignore Jinnah's points in the same manner she ignores you 😔.
  • S C Bose, J L Nehru and Srinivasa Iyengar formed Indian Independence League in 1928. The league was formed in opposition to the Nehru Report.
  • Those in support of Simon Commission: B R Ambedkar and Hindu Mahasabha (founded in 1915 by Madan Mohan Malaviya).

§ 13FACTORS THAT LED TO CIVIL DISOBEDIENCE MOVEMENT

  • Calcutta Session, 1928: In this Session, Nehru Report was accepted.
  • Irwin's Declaration, 1929: This is also known as "Deepavali Declaration". Viceroy Lord Irwin promised Dominion status in the future and a Round Table Conference post-Simon Commission's Report.
  • Delhi Manifesto, 1929: It outlined several key conditions by Indian leaders' for participating in the Round Table Conference.
  • Lahore Session, 1929: It was presided by J L Nehru

Decisions taken:

  • 1st Round Conference Table to be boycotted.
  • Goal: "Purna Swaraj" (Complete Independence).
  • 31 Dec 1929: Flag was hoisted by J L Nehru on the banks of Ravi river with slogans of "Inquilab Zindabad".
  • 26 Jan 1930 was fixed as the First Independence Day.
  • Congress authorised to launch CDM.
  • Gandhi presented his 11 demands as an ultimatum before launching CDM.
  • Dominion Status was first demanded by Tej Bahadur Sapru and M R Jaykar
  • "Inquilab Zindabad" slogan was given by Hasrat Mohani

Participation of Leaders in Different States

  • Tamil Nadu: C Rajagopalachari (led Salt March from Trichinopoly to Vedaranniyam).
  • Malabar: K Kelappan.
  • Orissa: Gopalbandhu Choudhary.
  • Bihar: Ambika Kant Sinha (Nakhas Pond was chosen as a site to violate Salt Law).
  • Peshawar: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan or Badshah Khan or Frontier Gandhi.
  • He launched "Red Shirt Movement".
  • Established: Khudai Khidmatgar (Servants of God).
  • Dharsana: Sarojini Naidu, Imam Saheb and Manilal took up the unfinished task of Gandhi in Dharsana. Sarojini Naidu also persuaded Gandhi to seek women participation.
  • Kamala Devi Chattopadhyay famously said to Gandhi, "Do not restrict this movement to men alone".
  • Manipur and Nagaland: Rani Gaidinliu.

Forms of Mobilization

  • Prabhat Pheri, Vanar Sena, Manjari Sena were organised for mobilising the masses.

§ 14Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931

  • It was signed on 14 February between Gandhi and Irwin.

Irwin's demands to Gandhi:

  • Suspend CDM.
  • Participate in 2nd Round Table Conference.

Gandhi's demands (which were accepted by Irwin):

  1. 1. Release political prisoners, not convicted of violence.
  2. 2. Give the confiscated properties back to Indians which are not yet sold to third-parties.
  3. 3. Right to produce salt for personal consumption.
  4. 4. Right to make salt in coastal villages for personal consumption.

Gandhi's demands (which were not accepted by Irwin):

  1. 1. Public inquiry into police excesses.
  2. 2. Commutation of death sentence to Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, and Rajguru.

§ 15Karachi Session

  • It was held on 29 March 1931 → Presided by Sardar Patel.
  • Gandhi-Irwin Pact (or Delhi Pact) was accepted.
  • Congress agreed to participate in 2nd Round Table Conference
  • CDM was suspended.
  • The goal of Purna Swaraj was reiterated (for the first time meaning of Purna Swaraj was stated).
  • Two resolutions were adopted: Fundamental Rights and National Economic Policy.

§ 16Round Table Conference (RTC)

  • RTCs were held in London to discuss about Simon Commission Report and future reforms for the country.

§ 17CIVIL DISOBEDIENCE MOVEMENT

Dandi March

  • Dandi March was the beginning of Civil Disobedience Movement.
  • Time period: 12 March-6 April 1930.
  • Gandhi marched 241 miles along with 78 delegates from Sabarmati Ashram (Ahmedabad) to Dandi (Navsari) to violate Salt Law due to which it is also known as Salt Satyagraha.
  • Gandhi decided to raid Dharshana, Gujarat but Abbas Tyabji led the raid in Darashana Salt Works after the Gandhi was arrested on 4 May.
  • Salt was chosen as the theme because of the govt. tax on salt and its monopoly over its production which revealed govt.'s oppressive face.

Campaign across India

  • In Ryotwari Areas: Non-payment of revenue.
  • In Zamindari Areas: No chowkidar tax.
  • In Central Province: Violation of forest laws.

§ 183 RTCs were held:

  • 1st: Nov 1930-Jan 1931.
  • 2nd: Sep 1931-Dec 1931 (it is the only RTC where Gandhi and Congress participated).
  • 3rd: Nov 1932-Dec 1932.
  • B.R. Ambedkar attended all 3 RTCs.
  • 2nd RTC failed due to non-acceptance of demands of Congress by British Government. Due to which Congress decided on 29th Dec 1931 to resume the CDM. The then Viceroy Willingdon also refused a meeting with Gandhi. On 4th Jan 1932, Gandhi was arrested, finally on April 1934 Gandhi withdrew the CDM.

Le Saunders: MUJHE KYU TODA?

§ 19CIVIL DISOBEDIENCE MOVEMENT

§ 20COMMUNAL AWARDS

  • The Communal Award was announced by British Prime Minister Ramsay MacDonald on 16th August 1932. It is also known as MacDonald Award.
  • It recognised the "Depressed Classes" as minorities and provided them a separate electorate along with some other communities like Muslims, Sikhs, Christians, Europeans, and Marathas as well.
  • Mahatma Gandhi strongly opposed the separate electorate for Depressed Classes, viewing it as a threat to Hindu unity however B. R. Ambedkar supported the Award, as it ensured political representation and safeguarded the rights of the Depressed Classes.

Congress neither accepted nor rejected the Communal Award.

§ 21Poona Pact 1932

  • The Poona Pact was an agreement between Mahatma Gandhi and B. R. Ambedkar, signed on 24th September 1932, at Yerwada Central Jail in Pune.
  • While in prison, Gandhi announced a fast unto death till the time separate electorates were removed from the Award, which led to an agreement between Gandhi and Ambedkar that discarded the separate electorate.

Note: Madan Mohan Malaviya signed Poona Pact on behalf of Gandhi

Key Provisions for Poona Pact

  • No separate electorates for Depressed Classes.
  • Number of seats reserved for Depressed Classes would be increased.

§ 22Gandhi's Efforts against Untouchability

  • All India Anti-Untouchability League (1932): This League, founded by Mahatma Gandhi was later re-named as the Harijan Sevak Sangh.
  • Harijan (Weekly newspaper)

§ 23GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT 1935

1937 Elections

  • Provincial elections were held in British India according to GOI Act 1935. Elections were held in 11 provinces. Congress got majority in all except → Punjab, Bengal, and Sindh.

For provisions of GOI Act 1935 refer to chapter: "Important Acts" in Polity section.

§ 24CONGRESS SESSIONS

  • 1934: Congress Socialist Party was formed by J P Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, A N Dev, Minoo Masani.
  • 1936: Held in Lucknow; All Indian Kisan Sabha (AIKS) was formed by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati.
  • 1937: Faizpur → 1st session to be held in a village (Jalgaon, Maharashtra). This session was presided over by J L Nehru.
  • 1938: Haripura, Gujarat led by S C Bose (elected as President of INC) marked the beginning of growing ideological differences between Bose and Mahatma Gandhi, though the full rift developed in 1939 during the Tripuri Session.
  • National Planning Committee (NPC) was established in 1938 by S C Bose, during the Haripura Session. The first chairman of this Committee was J L Nehru.
  • 1939: Tripuri Session in Jabalpur (Madhya Pradesh) → S C Bose was re-elected as President of INC by defeating Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya, but later S C Bose resigned from Congress and he formed All India Forward Bloc, 1939, Unnao, Uttar Pradesh

§ 25World War II

  • In 1939, World War II began → It was fought between the Allied Powers (Britain, France, USA, USSR) and the Axis Powers (German, Italy, Japan).
  • In October 1939, the INC resigned from all provincial ministries to show protest against Britain's decision to involve India in World War II without consulting Indian leaders.
  • After resigning, the INC made offers to Vicerey Lord Linlithgow regarding India's involvement in World War II. The demands were:
  1. 1. Demand for establishment of Constituent Assembly to draft a Constitution for the Indian people
  2. 2. Demand for establishment of fully responsible Government at both Provincial and Central level

Autobiography of Hitler: Mein Kampf

§ 26AUGUST OFFER 1940

  • In 1940, August Offer was sent by Lord Linlithgow under the direction of British Prime Minister Winston Churchill to secure India's cooperation in World War II. The key Provisions were:
  1. 1. The British Government promised to grant Dominion Status for India.
  2. 2. Indians could create their own Constituent Assembly themselves with inclusion of more Indian representatives than whites.
  3. 3. An advisory war council was to be established.
  • → However these provisions were rejected by Congress as Congress had declared "Purna Swaraj" as their goal.

Revolutionary Socialist Party was established in 1940.

§ 27Individual Satyagraha 1940

  • The INC decided to launch the "Individual Satyagraha" after the failure of August Offer under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi in 1940 with Vinoba Bhave nominated as first Satyagrahi, J L Nehru as second and Brahma Dutt as the third.

§ 28CRIPPS MISSION 1942

  • In 1942, Stafford Cripps was sent to India with a constitutional reforms. The key proposals were:
  1. 1. A Constituent Assembly would be formed to frame a new constitution for the country. This Assembly would have members elected by the provincial assemblies and also nominated by Princely States.
  2. 2. India would be granted Dominion Status, allowing self-governance while remaining part of the British Commonwealth.
  3. 3. Any province unwilling to join the Indian dominion could form a separate union and have a separate constitution.
  4. 4. The transfer of power and the rights of minorities would be safeguarded.

§ 29QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT

The proposals were rejected by INC. Gandhi famously referred Cripps offer of Dominion Status as "post-dated cheque drawn on a failing bank".

§ 30QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT 1942

  • July 1942: The Congress Working Committee met at Wardha, Maharashtra where Quit India Resolution was adopted. It was ratified at Gowalika Tank, Bombay.

§ 31Quit India Movement

  • On 8th August 1942, Mahatma Gandhi launched Quit India Movement (also known as August Kranti) in response to the failure of Cripps Mission. which was initially not supported by J L Nehru and Hindu Mahasabha.
  • The "Do or Die" slogan was given during a speech by Mahatma Gandhi at the Gowalia Tank Maidan or August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai. The slogan was a call to action for Indians to fight for independence from British rule.
  • The very first day all leaders got arrested and that is why this movement was a leaderless movement.
  • Aruna Asaf Ali presided over Congress Working Committee, she also hoisted the Indian Flag at the Gowalika Tank in Mumbai.

§ 32Specific Appeals made by Gandhi (during the Quit India Movement):

  • To government servants Gandhi advised not to resign from their posts but instead urged them to remain loyal to the cause of the INC and work against British policies subtly.
  • Soldiers were instructed not to resign from their duties but were urged to refuse orders to fire on fellow compatriots.
  • Gandhi appealed to peasants to withhold rent payments if the landlords or Zamindars were loyal to the British government.
  • He encouraged the people living in princely states to support their ruler if the ruler was anti-British. If the ruler was pro-British, Gandhi advised them to peacefully oppose the government.

§ 33Martyrs

  • Kushal Konwar was the only martyr of the Quit India phase of the freedom movement who was hanged.
  • Kanaklata Barua was shot dead by the British forces while leading a procession during QIM.

§ 34Underground Activities Carried Out:

  • Usha Mehta: Launched underground radio in Bombay and appealed Indians to join Quit India Movement.
  • Parallel government were setup:
  • In Ballia by: Chittu Pandey
  • In Tamluk by: Jatiya Sarkar
  • In Satara by: Prati Sarkar (Y B Chauhan, Nana Patil)
  • 23 March 1943: Pakistan Day was observed by Muslim League.

The term PAKISTAN was coined in 1933 by Rahmat Ali

  • Lahore Resolution: It is also called as Pakistan Resolution was a formal political statement adopted by the All-India Muslim League on the occasion of its three-day general session in Lahore, Punjab, from 22 to 24 March 1940, calling for a separate homeland for the Muslims of British India.

§ 35Mediation between Congress and Muslim League

  • 1944: C. Rajagopalachari gave C R Formula (Clement-Read Formula) in response to the growing tensions between the INC and the Muslim League.
  • Desai Liaquat Pact 1945: It was an unsuccessful agreement between Bhalubhai Desai (from Congress) and Liaquat Ali Khan (from Muslim League).
  • 1945: Wavell Plan was proposed by then Viceroy Lord Archibald Wavell as an attempt to resolve the political deadlock between the INC and the Muslim League. This plan was discussed in Shimla Conference; however it failed.

In September 1945, World War II completely ended with the US bombings. In August 1945, US bombed in Hiroshima and Nagasaki (two cities of Japan) on 6 August and 9 August respectively. The bomb dropped on Hiroshima was known as "Little Boy". While the bomb dropped on Nagasaki was known as "Fat Man" which was more powerful than the "Little Boy" and that is from where we came up with the idea of naming this book and our GK MCQ Book (Little Boy).

§ 36INDIAN NATIONAL ARMY (INA)

  • The Indian National Army (INA) was founded during World War II to fight against British rule in India.
  • It was initially formed in 1942 by Mohan Singh with Indian Prisoners of Wars in Singapore (it was later handed to Rash Behari Bose who again transferred the leadership to S C Bose).

§ 37Subash Chandra Bose

  • He was born in Cuttack in 23rd Jan 1897.
  • In 1942, he met Hitler in Germany (he had earlier travelled to Berlin in April 1941 using the Italian passport of "Orlando Mazzotta").
  • The Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) was reorganised by Bose in Singapore in 1943.
  • He founded "Free India Legion/Tiger Legion" in 1941 in Berlin, Germany.
  • He formed a women regiment named after Rani Lakshmibai led by Captain Lakshmi Swaminathan.
  • On 15th August, Japan surrendered to Allied powers, marking the end of World War II.
  • He died on: 18th August in a plane crash.
  • S C Bose was called as "Patriot of Patriots" by Gandhi.
  • In 1944, he was the person to give "Father of Nation" title to Gandhi through Singapore Radio.

Birth anniversary of S.C. Bose is celebrated every year as "Parakram Diwas".

§ 38Famous Slogans by S C Bose

  • "Delhi Chalo"
  • "Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom"
  • "Jai Hind"

The Indian struggle 1920-1942 was authored by S C Bose.

§ 39QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT

§ 40INA trials

  • The Indian National Army trials (also known as the INA trials and the Red Fort trials) was the British Indian trial by court-martial of a number of officers of the Indian National Army (INA) between November 1945 and May 1946.
  • First INA trial was held against: Prem Kumar Sehgal, Shah Nawaz Khan and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon in Red Fort in 1945.
  • Congress came in defence of these INA soldiers and formed a committee which included Jawaharlal Nehru, Bhulabhai Desai, Asaf Ali, Tej Bahadur Sapru, Kailash Nath Katju, and others.
  • 14th February 1946: The ratings (sailors in lowest rank) of Royal Indian Navy (RIN) revolted against British due to the discrimination and poor conditions and this led to a historic Royal Indian Navy Mutiny. This event began at the HMIS Talwar (a shore establishment in Bombay) against the poor working conditions (low pay, poor food quality, etc.).

§ 41CABINET MISSION PLAN

  • In 1945, elections were held in Britain where Labour Party under the leadership of Clement Attlee formed the government.
  • In March 1946, Clement Attlee (then PM of Britain) sent a delegation called the Cabinet Mission consisting of:
  • Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Chairman), Sir Stafford Cripps and A. V. Alexander.
  • It proposed a 3-tiered Federal Plan.

§ 42Provisions in Cabinet Mission Plan

  • The plan proposed a united India, rejecting the demand for a separate Pakistan.
  • The Cabinet Mission Plan, proposed a three-tier administrative structure for British India, with the Federal Union at the top tier, individual provinces at the bottom tier and Groups of provinces as a middle tier.
  • Provincial were divided into three groups:
  • Group A: Hindu-majority provinces (Madras, Bombay, UP, Bihar, Odisha, Central Provinces)
  • Group B: Muslim-majority provinces (Punjab, NWFP, Sindh, Balochistan)
  • Group C: Bengal and Assam
  • Central Government to have power over defense, foreign affairs, and communications.
  • Provinces to have full autonomy and residual powers.
  • Princely States were free to negotiate their status, either to join with Britishers or Successor Governments.
  • Constituent Assembly to draft a new constitution: members would be elected by provincial assemblies.
  • Interim Government to function till the new constitution and government were formed.

§ 43Response to the Cabinet Mission Plan

  • Indian National Congress: It accepted the plan partially but opposed the idea of grouping, fearing it was a step toward partition.
  • Muslim League: It initially accepted the plan though it did not have a separate provision for Pakistan, thinking that the provision for grouping will provide it a separate Nation but when Jinnah sensed that this grouping is not mandatory then he called for "Direct Action Day".

The Muslim League Observed "Day of Deliverance" on 22 December 1939

§ 44MOUNTBATTEN PLAN

  • The Mountbatten Plan which formed the basis for Indian Independence Act proposed for the Partition of India into two Dominions namely India and Pakistan. That's why it is also known as Partition Plan.
  • Under this Plan, the Princely States were given the option to join either India or Pakistan or remain Independent.
  • Out of 565 Princely States, 563 joined either India or Pakistan and 3 did not join initially. They were: J & K, Hyderabad and Junagarh.

Note: To see Provisions of Indian Independence act 1947 refer to chapter "Important Acts" in Polity section.

  • Louis Mountbatten: Last Governor-General of India.
  • C. Rajagopalachari: Only Governor-General of independent India (because later this post was removed).
  • Bangladesh Liberation War in 1971 led to the separation of East Pakistan (now Bangladesh) from West Pakistan (now Pakistan). This war took place during the tenure of Indira Gandhi.
  • In 1972, the Shimla Agreement was signed by Indira Gandhi (then Prime Minister of India) and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto (then President of Pakistan) to restore peace between two countries. It has been suspended by Pakistan in a move of retaliation after India suspended Indus Water Treaty.

§ 45QUIT INDIA MOVEMENT

  • Mahatma Gandhi was in Noakhali (present day Bangladesh) on August 15, 1947, the day India gained independence.
